author: markchen90
text: @Thom_Wolf @ArashVahdat But running Gaussian noise through a 2D Fourier Transform gives Gaussian noise on all frequencies. So the denoising model trades off between generating low frequency content at large t and in generating high frequency content at small t. 2/ https://t.co/G4ZwoWauWu

author: markchen90
text: @Thom_Wolf It's the coarse-to-fine inductive bias. This is most clear if you look at what's happening in frequency space (@ArashVahdat has a great slide on this in his diffusion models tutorial): When you run an image through a 2D Fourier Transform, most responses are at low frequencies. 1/ https://t.co/x2HqJrGszj

author: markchen90
text: @mobav0 We also investigate several hyperparameters and design choices for the infilling augmentation. For instance, conditioning on cat(suffix, prefix) is more cache friendly for autocomplete applications, but it turns out that it outperforms cat(prefix, suffix) as well! 3/

author: markchen90
text: @mobav0 But it turns out that even when you train with 90% of data augmented for the infilling task, you don't lose any of the left-to-right text generation capabilities, measured across a large number of benchmarks. It's critical not to apply loss masking on the infilling examples. 2/ https://t.co/JpOfAa7vTg

author: markchen90
text: Really proud to highlight work by @mobav0 and Heewoo showing that LMs can learn to infill text *for free*. Usually, when training on a mixture of tasks for a fixed token budget, you expect worse results compared to training fully on one of the tasks. 1/

quoted.text:
Efficient Training of Language Models to Fill in the Middle

Shows that autoregressive LMs can learn to infill text after we apply a straightforward transformation to the dataset, which simply moves a span of text from the middle of a document to its end.

https://t.co/4AZjMXr79X https://t.co/BAKNBTLAAz

author: markchen90
text: AlphaCode is well-executed and contains some great ideas. But to contextualize, a rating of 1238 can be achieved by solving all of the "translate the problem statement into code" problems quickly (and none of the harder "create a clever algorithm" problems).

quoted.text:
I spent 1000s of hours on competitive programming (proof-link: https://t.co/8KkFvcaGz6). This makes me qualified to comment on #AlphaCode by @DeepMind  

The result is nice, the benchmark will be useful, some ideas are novel. But human level is still light years away.

1/n
